notes.title: Zugnaex is Free
notes.notes: [p]We have some good news and some bad news.[/p][p]First the bad news, [b]Zugnaex is free[/b]. The demon has escaped from its eternal prison. The apocalypse is upon us. But that's where you come in. Battle online with your friends to defeat the demon. Humanity is counting on it.[/p][p]And now the good news, [b]Zugnaex is free[/b]. We host the non-Steam version of the game on our Itch.io site. But now the Steam version is also free.[/p][p]And there's more good news. We have added Steam achievements for online play. They are a work-in-progress, but they work and reveal more about the gameplay and story. Check them out![/p][p]For our early adopters, if you are able, please be sure to play online to collect the "Join the battle" achievement. We're looking into some cool rewards for you in the future.[/p][p]Did you know? On this day in 2019, the horror-comedy [i]Ready or Not[/i] premiered in theaters. This movie inspired us to create our own twisted version inside Zugnaex called [b]Ready or Knot[/b]. It's a PvP battle mode with explosive consequences. The sequel, [i]Ready or Not 2: Here I Come,[/i] is coming to theaters on April 10, 2026. What new mode will the sequel inspire?[/p][p]See you all in battle![/p]

notes.title: The Summoning of Zugnaex
notes.notes:
[h2]Zugnaex awaits[/h2]
These notes cover changes made over the last 6+ months. The game was revamped to address many concerns, the service was improved to better support players from around the world, and the story has progressed. Players are battling as we speak in preparation for the ultimate confrontation with Zugnaex. The time is now to prove yourself in battle and save humankind.

[h2]Client Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed & improved IWAD verification and search. The client will find compatible games installed with Steam.
[*] Improved stability. Fixed several issues that could cause a client crash. Please continue to report any issues you find.
[*] Added an example battle to the distribution. It's called "Kneed Time." You must finish a random UV E1 map in par. The instructions for how to build the client and server and setup the battle (a python program) are included in the README files.
[*] The client now checks for the best game server to connect to based on network speed. We hope you enjoy this performance improvement.
[*] There is no more login or account needed to battle online. You can set a username or leave it blank to get a random name.
[/list]
[h2]Battle Changes[/h2]
Many balance and gameplay changes have been made to the different battle modes. This is based on player feedback. These are the most significant changes noted below.
[h3][i]A Demon a Day[/i][/h3]
You battle demons with your friends to try to become a demon slaying legend. The lobby time has now been reduced. Grab what you can and get out to start the battle. Friendly fire is also back on now so be careful to not hit your allies (or maybe you're going for your own high score...)
[h3][i]Pennies from hell[/i][/h3]
Demons drop pennies and you collect them to get the highest score. It's PvP so everyone is out for themselves. There is now a weapon choice depending on which portal you use to enter the battle. The bonuses for secrets and level exit were increased. Exit bonus is scaled based on par time.
[h3][i]That Guy[/i][/h3]
You work together with your friends to complete different mission objectives. But there's a twist. The marines may succumb to the will of the demons and now must prevent others from finishing the tasks. The item respawn delays were increased to make the item task more challenging. You also have less time in the lobby to load up so be quick and selective.

[h2]The Summoning[/h2]
We're in the first stage of the summoning. Players are battling to earn an advantage and develop the skills needed to defeat Zugnaex.

notes.title: Important Community Update
notes.notes:
[h3]Initial release[/h3]
The initial release of [i][b]Zugnaex[/b][/i] on Steam raised many concerns within the DOOM®(1) community. When the game went live last year, it included Freedoom(2) assets, didn't disclose how AI was used, and caused anger by charging for something that made use of freely available code and assets. Years of work developing this tech, the battle modes, and the online service were all devalued. So I retired it.

[h3]Developer response[/h3]
I spent the next several months revamping the game. All Freedoom(2) assets were removed. The store page was rewritten to try to exactly describe the game. Details were added about the included source code. AI usage was fully disclosed. A standalone battle example was included that players could use to run their own battles. The backend service was upgraded to improve the gameplay experience for players around the world. And many more changes including bug fixes, performance improvements and new battle modes.

[h3]Community concerns continue...[/h3]
However, there are still concerns from the community. I want to hear those concerns, but action must be taken regarding the misinformation and negative comments. I understand why they are here. But I have acted on that feedback. I’m asking the community to respect that and continue to provide actionable, constructive and informational feedback based on the game as it is today.

[h3]Why are you charging for something that uses free code?[/h3]
This is a deep question. It’s about understanding the difference between free and freedom. In my opinion, the  Free Software Foundation (FSF)(3) promotes freedom but understands that there is a cost associated with software development. In the case of this game, in addition to thousands of hours spent developing the software, there is also a cost to operate the online service. I felt it was fair and reasonable to charge a fee for the Steam distribution. Whether it can cover operational costs or not, as long as players are playing, I’ll try my best to keep it running.

[h3]Why should we buy something you used AI to create?[/h3]
This entire mod was developed and initially released in the summer of 2022 with no AI usage at all. It was only in the last 1.5 years or so of development that I started using AI. I used it to help create the initial store page and that was a huge mistake for many reasons but mainly because it was not me. You learn from mistakes and move on. I continue to use AI tools but with much more restraint. As I am a programmer by trade, I didn’t use AI to generate the code in this mod. I wrote it. I did use AI to help answer technical questions which allowed me to write the code more efficiently.

There was a recent discussion on x.com (4) related to AI where two iconic figures in FPS history made some very strong comments on AI that are relevant here. They both happen to be programmers too, which is also interesting.

In response to a post discussing this recent AI tech demo,

[i]“Microsoft has created an AI-generated replica of Quake II that you can play in browser.”[/i]
-- Geoff Keighley [url=https://x.com/geoffkeighley/status/1908593030141202635](link to full post)[/url] (4)
 
Both John Carmack & Tim Sweeney shared their thoughts on modern AI.

[i]“AI tools will allow the best to reach even greater heights, while enabling smaller teams to accomplish more, and bring in some completely new creator demographics.”[/i]
-- John Carmack [url=https://x.com/ID_AA_Carmack/status/1909311174845329874](link to full post)[/url] (4)

[i]“AI will ultimately be a powerful tool in the toolbox of every programmer, artist,  and designer, just as high level languages, paint programs, and visual scripting were in previous eras. The opportunities available to everyone should ultimately increase as a result.”[/i]
-- Tim Sweeney [url=https://x.com/TimSweeneyEpic/status/1909313620540113087](link to full post)[/url] (4)

[h3]How can I use this tech to make something cool?[/h3]
Great question! The goal of this tech was to allow other modders to bring their stories online. It’s not there yet but with community support, it will happen!

---

[i][b]Do you have more questions, comments or concerns?[/b]
Post and I’ll try to answer them...

Otherwise, please help. [b]Zugnaex[/b] grows stronger as we speak. Only together can we defeat the demon and save humanity! See you in battle.[/i]

notes.title: Zugnaex Returns!
notes.notes:
We have some good news. Zugnaex is back! But don't panic. It's better than ever thanks to some really good advice from you all. Over the last few months, we completely revamped the game. The store page was redone. The service was improved so now players from around the world will have a better gameplay experience. Also, we're sharing the backstory and more.

[h3]What is Zugnaex?[/h3]
In the story, Zugnaex is a powerful demon. Players complete different challenges online to ultimately face and defeat the demon. When you install the game, "zugnaex.exe" is the program you run to play single player or battle online. It is a modification of a modification of a modification of (and so on and so forth) the 1993 DOOM® source code. Over the last 30+ years many talented developers have modified that code, created powerful tools, and updated it to keep up with modern game engines. The unique feature of Zugnaex is a bit confusing. What this mod does is it adds multiserver support. That means a player can travel from one server to another.

[h3]We've already got multiplayer so what makes this different?[/h3]
In traditional client/server multiplayer games you play on one server. When the match ends, the server changes maps. In multiserver games, when you exit a map you "zone" (in this context, this means travel to another server). An important aspect is the servers are managed by an external program that maintains player state (stats like health, armor, ammo, etc.). When you travel to another server, you keep your stats. This creates a seamless experience. It feels like a single WAD (game data file) but it's many of them.

[h3]What challenges await for me online?[/h3]
Great question! The online service hosts many battle variations. We are constantly working on new ones and making improvements to the ones that are available now. Here are some that you can experience:

[i]A Demon a Day[/i] - work together with your friends to defeat demons. Each kill counts for all active players but be careful as friendly fire is enabled. Help each other to get the highest score and become a demon slaying legend.

[i]That Guy[/i] - complete different mission objectives with your friends but there's a twist. The demons are powerful and the marines may succumb to their will. Who is your ally and who is your enemy? Play to find out.

[i]Pennies from hell[/i] - this is a parody. Demons drop pennies and you collect them. It's a PvP party where the best players will wallow in the riches offered by the denizen of hell.

[i]Ready or Knot[/i] - it's time to play hide & seek but old school FPS style. It's PvP where all players are against "it." If "it" survives the other players explode just like in the movie.

And many more including speed running, co-op adventures and the ultimate confrontation with Zugnaex itself.
